GTA IV was updated recently to remove GFWL so players can play it without having the need to login or use the client while saving their games. However, Rockstar have forgotten to remove GFWL in EFLC. This may be seen as an issue but it can be easily fixed by downloading the Xliveless client from the internet which will fix the saving feature in EFLC. You will be able to play the game normally by obtaining the client. It's a shame that Rockstar forgot about updating EFLC.

Other than that, EFLC is an amazing expansion to the rich writing of GTA IV and I can always recommend it to anyone who has played IV first. If you don't play IV it may be a bit difficult to understand certain areas of the storylines in EFLC. I'd suggest you play IV before playing TBOGT or TLAD. I really like TBOGT the most out of this expansion, it's like the opposing force to Half-life, an expansion which adds in a new amount of great features and story.

I'd heard that [i]TLAD[/i] was mediocre and paled in comparison to the base game and [i]The Ballad of Gay Tony[/i], but I actually liked it a lot more than the base game.

+ Johnny handles motorcycles way better than Niko handles cars
+ There aren't any [i]really[/i] bad bikes (while most of the cars are terrible)
+ You can get bikes for free and guns at a discount whenever you want by calling your gang members
+ At the end of an early mission, [spoiler]the game tries to make you think it's gonna go all [i]San Andreas[/i] and let your gang get pushed around by a couple of corrupt cops, but you just go kill them in the next mission[/spoiler]
+ You don't get called to go do things with your friends all the time
+ This game introduces the sawn-off shotgun, which is the most hilariously overpowered gun to use on a motorcycle
+ Also introduces a few more guns that are more interesting than anything in [i]GTA IV[/i]: An automatic pistol, a street sweeper shotgun and a grenade launcher
+ I enjoy playing as bikers in games and Johnny has a sweet jacket

/ The story is still generally joyless
/ The story is short, but there are a lot of side jobs, gang wars and races to do as well
/ Johnny flipping his shit in combat for little reason can be alternately hilarious and annoying. "F*** YOU! [b]F*** [i]YOU![/i][/b] F*** YOU F*** YOU F*** YOU F*** YOU!" (this is all one line)

- Only 2 safehouses, both very close together, and you can only use one or the other for most of the plot
- Johnny runs slower than Niko and Luis if he's holding a weapon
- The bike handling is still iffy, and the 4-wheeled vehicle handling is iffy at [i]best[/i]
- The death metal station has like 8 songs on it so if you listen to it a lot it will repeat all the time
- No character customization

[i]TLAD[/i] is still no [i]San Andreas[/i] or [i]Vice City[/i] but it's a pretty good game.

[h1]The Lost and Damned[/h1]

This episode focuses on motorcycles, as you would expect from a game that revolves around a biker gang. If GTA4 wasn't gritty enough for you, this one's even grittier. Storywise, it's about the same level of grittiness as GTA4, if not more, If you like riding bikes, you'll like this episode; Johnny Klebitz has mastered the delicate art of not flying off his bike when clipping a lamp post at 20 miles an hour. Though he's not as good of a driver as Niko, and you'll definitely notice that if and when you get behind the wheel. There's more content in general, including an exclusive set of weapons to play with, including an autopistol, a sawed-off shotgun, and a grenade launcher. You get all three of these pretty damn early in the game; the sawed-off is Johnny's starter weapon and he can fire it while riding! Worth playing if you want to follow a parallel, equally if not more gritty story to Niko's.

Lost MC! Lost MC!



[h1]The Ballad of Gay Tony[/h1]

This episode takes a leap away from GTA4's usual brand of grittiness; it's more colorful, has lots of new fun guns to play with (P90 SMG, advanced sniper rifle, M249 light machine gun, AA-12 shotgun with explosive rounds...), parachutes, upgraded police units, and a whackier tone to compete with its new nemesis, Saints Row 2. This one focuses a bit more on helicopters, so this episode may be good practice for the awful PC controls for the helicopters. Or it may frustrate you a bit. Once you finish the story, you can go back and replay any mission you want. There's a score system for missions this time around, but who cares? I actually find this episode to be more fun than GTA4 just because of all the fun stuff it adds. There's nothing like screwing up everyone's commute in Star Junction with stickybombs and an explosive shotgun. What's that? The police are coming? Pfft. They ain't got shit on my APC.

You'll have a good time. And as always, mods only increase the fun.

Grand Theft Auto: Episodes from Liberty City is an expansion pass for GTA 4 where you have to DLC packs which both expand on the story of GTA 4. I will review both as separate games so let's get into it.

Grand Theft Auto Lost and Damned:

This expansion pass follows on the biker gang Lost and Damned who are old school gang in Liberty City. The story follows on Johny Klebitz as he tries his best to keep his chapter under falling out.

This expansion is really good, for story, but not so much for missions. 

Now I know that I should have expected this, from an expansion that follows on Bikers, but I didn't really like how much of the entire expansion follows on bike rides. But the story missions were fun and challenging.

Music wise I enjoyed the rock music in this game, it's a very fitting choice of music for this expansion and it works well.

The entire expansion overall is still better than the entirety of GTA 4, I enjoyed the story and action based missions, but hated all the bike stuff, because of how bikes control in GTA 4 overall.

Next up is Grand Theft Auto The Ballad of Gay Tony:

This expansion is better than Lost and Damned and GTA 4.

This expansion follows on Luis a bodyguard who works on a business man Gay Tony. The entire expansion takes place after the Three Leaf Clover mission in GTA 4 and is all about Luis trying to save Tony's dying business by taking up different business ventures.

This expansion is incredibly fun and I had tons of fun playing through it. A lot of the missions are really fun action packed missions and it fixes a lot of the problems that Lost and Damned and GTA 4 had.

The overall atmosphere is also not as dark and lightens the tone. It's also incredibly funny, the characters are funny and it's all really fun. 

Lightening the tone also helps a lot, cause GTA 4 being way too serious made the game kind of boring to play. 

This expansion also paves the way to GTA 5 like the medals in missions and multiple characters.

Overall this expansion is a great addition and is overall better than the main game, but I still suggest playing all three games.

Pros:
+ Funny and cleverly written stories
+ Missions are action packed so it never gets boring to play
+ Soundtracks which fit the overall atmosphere of the expansions

Cons:
- Gameplay and Car physics aren't that good
- Gun gameplay is incredibly stiff

Final Rating:
9/10

As I write this, the release date for GTA V is fast approaching. Hard to believe it's been 5 years since GTA4 was released.

GTA: Episodes from Liberty City (EFLC) moves the base GTA4 game forward nicely. There's two smaller storylines, each about 12-16 hours of gameplay. Both stories are interwoven with the main GTA4 storyline. Niko Bellic and other characters make appearances in these games, and certain loose ends are tied up in these episodes.

The stories are strong, the supporting characters are interesting, and the protagonists are fun to play. Luis Lopez, the main character in The Ballad of Gay Tony, is my new favorite GTA protagonist - even better than Vice City's Tommy Vercetti. These two smaller games are much more interesting to me than Niko Bellic's story.

EFLC delivers some technical fixes and gameplay improvements to the base game.  Most notably, we now have mid-mission checkpoints, so if you fail a mission, you can pick up part-way through. This really decreases the frustration level of the game. Less notably, but important to me: traffic is more realistic. And, motorcycles are easier to control.

The Ballad of Gay Tony is the standout episode. It brings back the over-the-top flavor of Vice City and San Andreas. The missions are crazy fun, including a shootout on top of the Empire State Building, hijacking a subway car, helicopter duels, and a race around Manhattan -- excuse me, "Algonquin" -- involving parachutes, speedboats and fast cars. There's a new cage-fighting mini-game, and everywhere you turn in this one, there's fast cars to boost. And, as mentioned, parachuting! There's 20 optional missions involving base jumping and parachuting skills. Excellent fun. The Ballad of Gay Tony pulls out all the stops to show off what this game engine is capable of delivering. And maybe, hopefully, it shows that Rockstar hasn't forgotten how to have fun. 

If you need a GTA fix before GTA V appears and you skipped these episodes, you should definitely take a second look.

Edit:

I felt inclined to update this review after finding out a little more about the graphics settings for this game. GTA IV is not necessarily meant to be maxed out on current hardware, the intention of the developers was that the higher graphical settings would be for future use, and when GTA IV was released on PC back in 2008 there was a disclaimer of some sort that advised players to use medium settings. I'm just learning this now and I had purchased GTA IV in 2012. People are criticizing the game for being a terrible port and having framerate issues because they believe they should be able to max out a 7 year old game. In most cases they would not be wrong in assuming that, but gta iv does have higher minimum requirements than pretty much any other game. Now, with current patches, as long as you have this game configured correctly it will run beautifully.

AUTO CONFIGURE IS YOUR FRIEND.

Use it when you are tweaking your graphics. If you have a decent rig, most of the settings will be automatically set to high/very high, except for VD, DD, and Vehicle Density. If you want to push it further, I would increase the vehicle density, which has the lowest impact on framerate, and you will be all right leaving everything else alone. Hope this helps anyone thats having trouble running this game.

Last time I played was in Windows 7 and it worked fine, but getting it working in Windows 10 was kind of a pain. I could always play it in Windows 7 by putting GFWL on offline mode, but this time there doesn't seem to be an offline option.

First of all, install "Games For Windows Marketplace" (google it, should be the first result, xbox.com page), set up an account if you don't have one. The game may automatically direct you to the download link upon trying to launch it for the first time, it did for me. You may get a prompt from Windows 10 that it's not compatible, but install it anyway. Without Games For Windows Live/Marketplace installed, the game won't launch at all.

Make sure you put "-nomemrestrict -norestrictions" (without quotes of course) in the game's launch options (right click it in Steam library, select Properties). If you don't, the game won't let you change resolution or any graphics settings.

From the main menu, pick the LIVE option and sign in. It may take a while, maybe not, but just be patient if it seems to take a while. At some point it will also ask for your game key. Don't try to close the GFWL overlay in the game while it's signing in either, I did and the whole thing became unresponsive.

It may ask you to update GFWL, I updated but it may not be necessary. If you choose to update, it will ask you to exit and re-launch the game, just sign in again from the main menu using the LIVE option. When I tried to sign in when prompted while starting a new game, it crashed. So using the LIVE option from the main menu was necessary for me. It will also download your "Profile" this may also take a bit, again just be patient.

Once you're signed into LIVE go ahead and start a new game, it should work without any problems.

TL;DR

To get EFLC working in Windows 10:

1) Install Games For Windows Marketplace, sign up for an account if you don't have one.
2) Put "-nomemrestrict -norestrictions" (without quotes) in launch options for game.
3) Launch game, set up graphics, sign into GFWL using the "LIVE" option in the main menu. It may take a while, be patient. It may ask for the game key, just put it in and it will work.
4) Start a new game.

Episodes from Liberty City é um pacote com as duas expansões de GTA 4, inicialmente lançadas separadamente, sendo que podem ser jogadas mesmo sem possuir o jogo de base. Ambas trazem pequenas variações no mapa em relação ao original e algumas pequenas novidades.

O primeiro episódio, The Lost and Damned, diz respeito a uma gangue de motoqueiros que teve seu líder (Billy Grey) capturado pela polícia. Até que ele pudesse retornar, a gangue passou a ser comandada por Johnny Klebitz que guiou seus companheiros à prosperidade.

No entanto, anos se passaram e com o retorno de Billy, ele estava totalmente transformado de forma que sua liderança estava destruindo tudo que havia sido construído e pondo em risco seus membros. Esta situação faz com que alguns dos membros se revoltem.

Nesta expansão, o jogador controla Johnny, que por sinal se movimenta muito devagar, bem mais devagar que Nicko. Como há um maior foco em motocicletas, foram acrescentados alguns modelos novos e tornou-se praticamente impossível cair delas.

Uma coisa ruim é que as vozes dos motoqueiros não combinam com os personagens e nos faz ter dificuldade de saber quem é quem está falando, o que prejudica um pouco o entendimento dos diálogos.

Já o segundo episódio, The Ballad of Gay Tony, assumimos o papel de Luis Lopez, braço direito de Tony Prince, um vi4dinho dono das melhores boates em Liberty City. Luis é sócio de Tony e eles são apenas amigos, sendo que não há nenhuma outra relação entre eles.

Diferente dos outros personagens, Luis vive na vida boa, tem um bom apartamento e várias mulheres. O problema é que o negócio das boates já não está tão lucrativo como antes, e seu mentor Tony se meteu em algumas enrascadas tentando diversificar os investimentos.

The Ballad of Gay Tony tem as melhores músicas tocando nas rádios contando todos os GTA’s já lançados, pelo menos na minha opinião, além de missões frenéticas e um sistema de pontuação por missão que premia o jogador em realiza-las usando métodos específicos.

Há nas duas expansões algumas adições muito bem vindas, como um sistema de checkpoints nas missões em que, no caso de falha, o jogador não precisa repetir a missão desde o começo, mas sim do último checkpoint.

Também foram adicionados novos mini games, como queda de braço e competição de bebida, corridas com bastões e habilidade para dançar. Foi retirada (felizmente) a necessidade de ficar ligando para as pessoas para manter relacionamentos.

O interessante é que as tramas das expansões ocorrem paralelamente a do jogo principal, sendo que por várias vezes passamos pelo mesmo local onde ocorreu algum evento e podemos ver os personagens dos outros jogos realizando as ações que fizemos, quando estávamos jogando com eles.

Além disso, as histórias são interligadas, com várias referencias cruzadas, e há situações em que realizaremos missões  com a participação dos personagens dos outros jogos, o que nos ajuda a entender melhor qual o que ocorreu em cada evento.

Algo que já acontecia no GTA 4 original, mas agora é muito frequente é o recebimento de alguma ligação que faz iniciar uma missão qualquer... Isso é muito chato porque não há como não aceitar e você deverá fazer aquela missão compulsoriamente naquele momento, mesmo que tivesse em mente fazer outra coisa.

Não se pode deixar de mencionar que também foram herdados alguns bugs do título principal, mas pelo menos são bem menos numerosos, e não atrapalham tanto jogar como eram naquele, de forma que não há quase nada para reclamar do jogo.

No fim das contas, se você jogou GTA 4, é praticamente obrigatório que você jogue suas expansões também, pois são bastante sólidas e talvez até mais divertidas que o título principal. EXCELENTE (9/10).

General Overview

Grand Theft Auto: Episodes from Liberty City is an expansion pack for Grand Theft Auto IV and while you don't need to own the base game to play, I would recommend you play through that first so the narrative makes more sense and you will also see how all three stories from each of the characters connect and intertwine with one another which I found to be interesting.

The Lost and Damned

In the first story, you play as protagonist Johnny Klebitz - a man who is second in command of a notorious biker gang known as The Lost. There are 22 missions in total with three (or four) random character missions. This will take you around 10 or 15 hours to complete depending how much you focus on the storyline. There are mid-mission checkpoints which were not present in the base game and also new weapons including the sawn-off shotgun, assault shotgun, pool-cues, grenade launchers and pipe bombs. New vehicles include Johnny's custom-made Hexer motorcycle among other bikes not found in the original game. You will also be able to call on your Lost brothers for bikes, backing you up and discounted weapons or just to hang out. Gang wars and bike races are the unique activities included in this episode. Activities you can play with your Lost brothers which were not present in the base game are arm wrestling, hi-lo cards and ever air hockey! Several new songs are added to the radio stations in TLAD - LCHC (Liberty City Hardcore) and Liberty Rock Radio saw the biggest additions of tracks to fit in with the expansion's biker theme in particular. The story itself is dramatic, the voice acting is excellent and motorcycle mechanics have been vastly improved.

The Ballad of Gay Tony

In the second story, you take control of protagonist Luis Fernando Lopez. An ex-member of the Dominician drug dealers and personal bodyguard of Anthony "Gay Tony" Prince. "Gay Tony" is a name well known throughout Liberty City and very high up on the social ladder as owner of the two biggest nightclubs in the city. Throughout the story, Luis has to aid Tony in battling drugs, debt, mafia families and attempts on both of their lives. This expansion contains roughly the same amount of missions as TLAD but once you complete the main story, you can choose to replay any mission from your phone and depending on factors such as time taken, damage taken among other objectives, you will get a ranking. Like TLAD, you can call on friends to sell you discounted weapons or to provide you with vehicles (and more are added as you progress in the story but you cannot call on them for backup) New vehicles include a NOOSE tank and a small attack helicopter known as the buzzard. New side jobs in TBOGT include drug wars, base jumping (which introduces parachutes back into the series) taking on triathlon races, working on club management, teeing it up at the golf range and entering an underground fight tournament (did someone say Flight Club?)

In the clubs you can dance, take shots (get completely wasted and you will wake up somewhere random if you drink enough) and partake in champagne drinking contests. New weapons at your disposal include: advance smg, the gold smg, the advanced mg, the 44. pistol, the advanced sniper rifle and sticky bombs. The grenade launcher and assault shotgun from the previous episode also return but this time you have the option of equipping explosive rounds which up the havoc and are a lot of fun. The story is a blast to play and without spoiling anything not only connects together at a certain point like TLAD and the base game but also answers some previously unanswered questions which I found to be very satisfying. In TBOGT there is much more of a glitz and glamour feel not found previously.

Closing comments

I found both episodes highly enjoyable to play (although I will say I preferred TBOGT just a bit more) If you're looking for more GTA IV adventures you simply cannot go wrong with this and it concludes the GTA IV saga. While the story in both episodes may not take too long to complete depending on how much you focus on it, there are many other activities to participate in for both episodes. If you're not bothered about achievement hunting however, the main missions will be more than satisfying. In terms of the content included I can't fault Rockstar for anything in these two episodes. It caps off the magnficence of Liberty in GTA IV.
